newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian engineers protest over pay demands.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian engineers protest over pay demands.

text.p: Hundreds of Jordanian engineers staged a sit-in on Saturday and threatened a nationwide strike action over long-simmering pays demands.

Activists in the Islamist-dominated Engineers Union said the sit-in was the first step in a campaign they will escalate to a strike by 4,000 public sector engineers on March 22 if their pay demands are not met.

The union resumed talk of industrial action last week after accusing the government of not being serious about fulfilling a deal agreed to last October, which averted another threatened strike action.

That deal committed the government to reach a solution within three months. The engineers, who say their salaries are lower than they were 10 years ago in real terms, want substantial increases to the system of salary bonuses and benefits granted for length of service.
The union says the government has done nothing during this period to meet the demands.
The union is Jordan's largest with a total of more than 26,000 members.
Jordanian officials accuse the Islamist opposition of exploiting the dispute to gain popular support.
Over the past year Jordan has been swept by a wave of strike threats by public sector workers, who form nearly half of the estimated 900,000 strong workforce.
